meta.title: FICO: The Toll Booth and the Regulator
meta.dek: The stock is down 62% from last October as Washington puts a $1 rival on the same pricing grid. FICO says lenders still pull its score. What does $708 assume about the $10 toll?
meta.price_note: Oct 26, 2026 close, matched on Yahoo Finance and Motley Fool; about $704–710 in early trading Oct 27

verdict.sentence: The mortgage toll that lifted earnings 42% is frozen at $10 and under regulatory attack; at $708 the probability-weighted case returns [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, and even the Base earns less than that.
verdict.breaks_if: Q4 mortgage-origination revenue (Q3: ~$285M) falls below ~$250M, or FHFA and the GSEs require a two-bureau credit report, which cuts royalties per loan by a third.

call: The market has stopped paying for a second doubling, and that is reasonable. Mortgage royalties are 42% of revenue and about 55% of segment profit, and their growth this year was price: +97% on volume up a few percent. At $708 the price implies a Bear probability of only [[implied_bear]], against my 35%, so the stock is not pricing the break. After a 62% fall it prices roughly my Base, with 2031 owner earnings per share of about [[Priced-in.owner_eps]] ([[Priced-in.cagr]] a year). What the market has wrong is that this is cheap. My Base grows owner earnings per share 12% a year and still returns less than 13% once the multiple settles, because the toll is frozen at $10 in front of a $1 rival, Equifax guides mortgage volume down in 2027, and the pulls-per-loan question sits with the FHFA. The break-even Bear probability is [[breakeven_bear]]; I do not need to defend 35% for the verdict to hold. The one number that would shift me is the fiscal 2027 EPS guide on November 4 against the $47.24 consensus. A debt-funded buyback at $1,149 has also taken net debt to 3.7 times EBITDA ahead of a covenant step-down. Good business; the weighted case returns [[pw_return]] and clears 13% only at [[entry]].

tests.if_fail: cut Base 2031 owner earnings per share to $56, about 12% (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]]**, entry [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That the regulators leave the three-bureau report alone and certify direct licensing.
tests.test: by the Q1 FY2027 print (late January 2027), no FHFA or GSE requirement for a two-bureau report has been published, the DLP holds its GSE certification, and the Preferred Program is reported to cover at least half of tri-merge volume.
tests.if_fail: move 15 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That the balance sheet delevers on schedule.
tests.test: in the FY2026 10-K (mid-November) and the Q1 FY2027 10-Q, total debt of $5.35B or less at September 30 and net debt ÷ adjusted EBITDA of 3.4× or less at December 31 against the 4.0× limit, with no repurchases in either quarter.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test3.verb]]**; the Outsider grade stays Anti-Outsider.

return_math.price_implied: At 10%, spot needs 2031 owner earnings per share of [[Priced-in.owner_eps]] (non-GAAP EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]]), or [[Priced-in.cagr]] a year, at 19×.
return_math.epv: $359 a share on FY2026's owner earnings held flat ($35.93 ÷ 10%). Growth pays for 49% of today's price. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits 7% above it because it keeps earnings flat at 11×.
return_math.base_rate: Revenue of $2.5B puts FICO in the $2–3B bucket, where 50.7% of companies grew sales at least 5% a year in real terms over five years and 23.8% grew at least 10% ([`compounding.md`](../../frameworks/compounding.md)). The Bull's 9.2% nominal (about 6.7% real) clears the 5% floor, so it is plausible. The Base's 5.9% nominal (about 3.4% real) is below it, so it is probable. Tiers: Bull plausible, Base probable, Bear probable.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing at 8% in year six in the Base: the platform and other scores carry it while mortgage is flat, so the multiple is not doing the work. The risk is the reverse, that 19× is generous if the platform stalls.
return_math.rr_note: The ratio is flattered by a Bull worth 2.5× spot; the Bear sits 46% below spot, so the downside is large too.
